The plaintiff-respondent brought the aforesaid suit in 1982 on the averments, inter alia, that the predecessor-in-interest of defendant Nos. 1-4, Syed Abdul Ali, got the suit properly as permanent lessee of the Government; that upon his death defendants No 1-4 inherited the suit, property; that they entered into an agreement with the plaintiff on 6-7-73 for selling the suit property at a price of Taka 80,000.00 which was paid in its entirety at the time of execution of the deed of agreement; that it was stipulated that they (defendant Nos. 1-4) would retain possession of the disputed property for 8 years and if within that period they could return the consideration money, the purchaser (plaintiff) would take back the same and in case of their failure to return the consideration money within the stipulated time the defendants would be bound to execute and register a deed of sale in favour of the plaintiff; that on their failure to do so the plaintiff would be at liberty to get the kabala executed and registered through court within the next one year; that defendants Nos. 1-4 in fact, failed to perform their part of the contract and as a result the cause of action for the suit arose on 5-8-82 Hence the suit. 

 6. In this case, a concise statement was filed on behalf of respondent No.3, namely, Rana  Ali, daughter of lala Hakim Syed Abdul Ali, the original owner of the suit property. In the concise statement it has been clearly stated that the suit for specific performance of contract was decreed ex parte against defendant Nos.1-4 and the addresses of defendant Nos. 1-4 were shown at House No. 40, Road No. 6, Dhanmondi Residential Area, Dhaka although they were living at 11, Barin Bari Lal Lane, Calcutta. In view of the addresses given in the plaint the service of summons upon them was effected under Order 9 rule 5 of the Code by hanging at, Dhaka address. Respondent No. 3 having come to know of the ex parte decree passed in Title Suit No. 471 of 1990 (renumbered as Title Suit No. 286 of 1992) filed Miscellaneous Case No. 50 of 1994 under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the ex parte decree was set aside and subsequently the suit itself was dismissed on 23-4-96. In this appeal, leave was granted on    3-11-94 and during the pendency of the appeal the main suit out of which the present appeal arose had already been dismissed on 23-4-96. In view of this factual position, the present decree passed in suit for specific performance of contract is no longer in existence. Thus the present decree passed in the suit cannot exist in view of dismissal of the original suit. Two conflicting decrees cannot co-exist in the same suit.
